correctness.rationale: Explicit algebra gives the critical height p_c and central fixed point a; the central branch is exactly affine with slope ±R and the outside points converge to zero. For R≤2, a forward-invariant constant-slope core has entropy log R. For R>2, two disjoint affine inverse branches yield a full two-shift and Hausdorff dimension log2/log R, and direct cylinder lengths give the precise survival/exit law. The global unimodal lap bound gives h≤log2; monotone trapping yields zero entropy for p≥p_c. Symbolic identities and hundreds of exact rational cylinders were checked by the embedded program. Boundary R=2 and p=p_c are treated separately.

value.rationale: The all-parameter law resolves the natural analytic boundary problem visible in a published Type-1 tent-composition numerical study. The sharp entropy jump, exact log2 plateau with an almost-sure zero basin in its strict interior, and Cantor dimension/escape law illuminate a robust topological-versus-physical complexity distinction. The results are not arbitrary numerical slices or textbook substitutions; they characterize the full stated three-parameter phase.
